name: Resolution Consistency
description: Analyzes DPI/resolution metadata vs actual pixel dimensions, checks for AI model-specific output sizes, and validates EXIF image size declarations against actual dimensions.
mechanism:
The resolution consistency analysis examines multiple signals:

1. **AI Model Resolution Matching**: Checks image dimensions against known AI model outputs (Stable Diffusion: 512², 768², 1024²; DALL-E 3: 1024×1024, 1792×1024; Midjourney: various).

2. **VAE Latent Space Detection**: Validates if dimensions are multiples of 64 (8× downsampled VAE latent space), which is characteristic of diffusion models.

3. **DPI Metadata Validation**: Cross-checks declared DPI (72 web, 96 screen, 240/300 print) against actual pixel dimensions. Inconsistencies suggest post-processing.

4. **EXIF Dimension Cross-check**: Compares ExifImageWidth/ExifImageHeight with actual decoded image dimensions to detect resizing.

5. **Megapixel Analysis**: Compares total pixel count against typical camera sensor outputs vs AI model capabilities.
parameters:
AI model resolutions: SD 1.x (512²), SD XL (1024²), DALL-E 3 (1024², 1792×1024), Flux (1024²)
DPI standards: 72 (web), 96 (screen), 240/300 (print)
VAE alignment: multiples of 64
Camera megapixels: 12-108 MP typical
accuracy: Medium - 70-80%. Most effective for unresized AI outputs. Accuracy decreases significantly when images are resized or cropped.
source: Latent Diffusion Model Architecture, JEITA CP-3451C
useCase: Quick AI detection screening based on dimensional analysis. Particularly effective for batch processing where images haven't been resized from their original AI-generated dimensions.
strengths:
• Fast dimensional analysis with no pixel processing needed
• VAE alignment check is highly specific to diffusion models
• DPI metadata inconsistencies reveal post-processing
• EXIF dimension cross-check catches subtle resizing
• Effective for identifying specific AI model outputs
limitations:
• Easily defeated by resizing or cropping the image
• Many camera resolutions overlap with AI model outputs
• Social media platforms resize images automatically
• Upscalers change dimensions to non-standard sizes
• DPI metadata is often inaccurate or absent

references.title: Rombach, R. et al. (2022). High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models. CVPR.
Podell, D. et al. (2023). SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis.
